question: How much does replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raise the solids content of NMC 532 slurries, and by what share does the higher solids content cut the primary drying time of the graphite coating?
rendered:
[background] Replacing the polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) binder with PVDF latex and carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) increases the solid content from 45 wt% to 65 wt% without increasing the slurry viscosity, allowing similar coating parameters to be used.

[background] In addition, the higher solid content dramatically shortens the primary drying time (i.e. from 51 s to 34 s for a graphite coating with a loading of 10 mg/cm^2) [37].

The solids content is raised by 20 wt% (65 wt% - 45 wt%). 
The primary drying time is cut by 33.33% ((51 s - 34 s) / 51 s).
